stem: The school hall ____ as a shelter last month.

options.feedback: 'Last month' is finished past time, so 'be' must be past: was used.
Correct: the hall received the action, and 'last month' needs the past simple: was + used.
be + V-ing means the hall was doing the using. The hall received the action: was used.
'Last month' is finished time, so the present perfect does not fit: was used.

hint: Ask two questions: did the hall do the action or receive it? When did it happen?
why: The hall received the action (people used it), and 'last month' is finished time, so we need the past simple passive: was + used.

stem: Every year, thousands of sandbags ____ along the river in Ayutthaya.

options.feedback: The sentence has no main verb. Add be: are placed.
After be, use the past participle (V3), not the base form: are placed.
Correct: a regular action, plural subject, and the sandbags receive it: are + placed.
be + V-ing means the sandbags are doing the placing. They receive the action: are placed.

hint: 'Every year' tells you the tense. Can sandbags do this action themselves?
why: 'Every year' needs the present simple. Sandbags cannot place anything, so the passive is needed: are + V3 (placed).

stem: Look! The fallen trees on our soi ____ right now.

options.feedback: This says the trees are removing something. They are receiving the action: are being removed.
Without 'been' this is active: the trees removed something. Trees cannot do that.
Correct: happening now + receiving the action = present continuous passive: are being + V3.
'Look!' and 'right now' mean the present, not the past: are being removed.

hint: 'Look!' and 'right now' tell you the tense. Can trees remove anything?
why: The action is in progress now and the trees receive it, so we need the present continuous passive: are + being + removed.

stem: Since Monday, more than 300 families ____ in the temple on higher ground.

options.feedback: Without 'been' this is active: the families housed someone. Add been: have been housed.
'Since Monday' joins the past to now, so it needs the present perfect, not the past simple.
The subject is 'families' (plural), so use have, not has.
Correct: 'since Monday' needs the present perfect, and families is plural: have been housed.

hint: 'Since' needs a particular tense. Check the subject: one family or many?
why: 'Since Monday' needs the present perfect. The families receive the action, and the subject is plural: have + been + housed.

stem: These flood barriers ____ in Japan and shipped to Thailand in 2025.

options.feedback: The sentence needs a main verb. Barriers cannot make anything: were made.
After be, use V3, not the base form: were made.
Correct: the barriers received the action in the past: were + made (and shipped).
be + V-ing means the barriers were making something. They were made.

hint: The second verb is 'shipped'. Did the barriers make anything?
why: The barriers received both actions in 2025, so both verbs are past simple passive: were made and (were) shipped.

stem: The bridge in our village ____ in 1995 and is still strong today.

options.feedback: A bridge cannot build anything. It needs be + V3: was built.
Correct: past simple passive with the irregular V3 'built'.
After was, use the past participle 'built', not the base form.
'Build' is irregular: build – built – built. There is no 'builded'.

hint: 'Build' is an irregular verb. What is its third form?
why: In 1995 is finished past time and the bridge received the action. 'Build' is irregular: build – built – built, so: was built.

stem: By the time the rain stopped, most of the stalls at the market ____.

options.feedback: Without 'been', the stalls damaged something. Add been: had been damaged.
be + V-ing means the stalls were doing the damage. They received it.
Correct: before a past moment ('the rain stopped') = past perfect passive: had been + V3.
'By the time the rain stopped' points to a past moment, so use had, not have.

hint: 'By the time' + a past verb means 'before that moment in the past'. Which tense shows that?
why: The damage happened before a past moment (the rain stopped), so we need the past perfect passive: had + been + damaged.

stem: Flood warnings ____ on the radio every hour yesterday.

options.feedback: 'Warnings' is plural, so use were, not was.
'Gave' is the past simple (V2). After be, use the V3: given.
Correct: plural subject, past time, passive: were + given.
be + V-ing means the warnings were giving something. They were given.

hint: Check the subject (one or many?) and the third form of 'give'.
why: 'Warnings' is plural and 'yesterday' is past, so we need were. After be we need the past participle of give: given.

stem: The drainage tunnel ____ twice since 2011, but it still overflows.

options.feedback: Without 'been', the tunnel repaired something. Add been.
'Since 2011' connects the past to now, so use the present perfect.
Correct: 'since 2011' + singular subject + passive: has been repaired.
'The drainage tunnel' is singular, so use has.

hint: 'Since 2011' tells you the tense. Is the subject singular or plural?
why: 'Since 2011' needs the present perfect, the subject is singular, and the tunnel received the action: has + been + repaired.

stem: Reports suggest that the warning ____ hours before the canal burst, but few residents saw it.

options.feedback: Without 'been', the warning sent something. A warning is sent: had been sent.
The canal burst in the past, so the present perfect cannot describe a time 'hours before' it.
Correct: sent before another past event (the canal burst) = past perfect passive.
This is active: the warning was sending something. Use had been sent.

hint: The canal burst in the past. Which happened first?
why: The warning was sent before another past event, and it received the action, so the past perfect passive fits: had + been + sent.

stem: The cause of the car fire ____ yet.

options.feedback: be + V-ing makes 'the cause' the doer. The cause is confirmed by investigators.
Without 'been', the cause confirmed something. Add been.
Correct: 'yet' + singular subject + passive: hasn't been confirmed.
'The cause' is singular, so use hasn't.

hint: 'Yet' goes with one tense. What is the real subject: the cause or the fire?
why: 'Yet' goes with the present perfect, the subject 'the cause' is singular, and someone confirms it: hasn't + been + confirmed.

stem: Which day ____ the shelter at our school opened last week?

options.feedback: 'Last week' needs the past: was.
'Did' needs a base verb (did … open). With 'opened' (V3) we need was.
'Last week' is finished time, so the present perfect does not fit.
Correct: past simple passive question: When was + subject + V3?

hint: Look at the verb form 'opened' and the time phrase 'last week'.
why: 'Last week' needs the past, and 'opened' here is a past participle, so the question is past simple passive: When was … opened?

stem: Free meals ____ to all displaced families at the shelter tomorrow.

options.feedback: This makes the meals the doer. Meals do not serve anyone: will be served.
'Will' needs be before the V3: will be served.
After be, use V3: will be served.
Correct: future passive: will be + V3.

hint: 'Tomorrow' gives the time. Can meals do this action themselves?
why: The future action is received by the meals, so we need will + be + V3: will be served.

stem: While the water level ____ every hour, villagers downstream were packing their belongings.

options.feedback: This is active: the water level checked something. It needs a passive.
This makes the water level the checker. It was being checked by officials.
'Were packing' is past, so the background action must be past too.
Correct: an action in progress in the past, received by the water level: was being checked.

hint: The other clause says 'were packing'. Which tense matches a background action in the past?
why: 'While' + 'were packing' shows two past actions in progress. The level received the action, so: was + being + checked.

stem: Many houses in Hat Yai ____ in the 2025 floods.

options.feedback: Houses cannot damage anything here. Add be: were damaged.
After were, use V3: damaged.
'Many houses' is plural, so use were.
Correct: plural subject + past + passive: were damaged.

hint: Check the subject (singular or plural) and the time.
why: The 2025 floods are in the past, 'houses' is plural, and the houses received the damage: were + damaged.

stem: The list of families who need emergency food and clean water ____ every morning.

options.feedback: Correct: the subject is 'the list' (singular), and it receives the action: is updated.
This makes the list the doer. Volunteers update the list: is updated.
The verb agrees with 'the list', not with 'families' or 'water'.
Without 'been' this is active. The list does not update anything.

hint: Find the head noun of the long subject. Is it singular or plural?
why: The head of the subject is 'the list' (singular), not 'families'. A routine action received by the list = present simple passive: is updated.

stem: Two new pumping stations ____ in our district next year.

options.feedback: After 'going to' you need be + V3: to be built.
This makes the stations the builders. They will be built.
'Two new pumping stations' is plural: are.
Correct: plan for the future + passive: are going to be built.

hint: A plan for next year. Can stations do this action themselves?
why: A future plan with a plural subject that receives the action: are going to + be + built.

stem: Our classroom ____ last Friday because the floor was muddy.

options.feedback: 'Was clean' only describes how it looked. 'Because the floor was muddy' explains an action: was cleaned.
Correct: someone cleaned the classroom last Friday: was cleaned.
This makes the classroom the cleaner. It was cleaned.
'Last Friday' is finished time, so use the past simple: was cleaned.

hint: The muddy floor is the reason for something. Was that an action or a description?
why: The muddy floor explains why something happened to the room, so we need an action received by the classroom: was + cleaned.

stem: The road to the hospital ____ since Saturday, so patients are taken there by boat.

options.feedback: 'Has closed since Saturday' is wrong: a sudden action cannot continue. The state continues: has been closed.
'Since Saturday' needs the present perfect.
Correct: a state from Saturday until now, and the road receives the action: has been closed.
'The road' is singular: has.

hint: 'Since Saturday' needs a tense that reaches the present.
why: The road has stayed closed from Saturday until now, so we need the present perfect passive of a state: has + been + closed.

stem: According to officials, about 329,000 households in Bangkok ____ by the floods.

options.feedback: Households did not affect anything. With 'by the floods' after the gap, use be + V3.
'Households' is plural: were.
Correct: past event, plural subject, agent 'by the floods' follows: were affected.
This makes the households the doers. They were affected.

hint: What comes after the gap? Who did the action?
why: The floods did the action and the households received it, so the passive is needed: were + affected (plural, past).

stem: Several cars were swept away ____ the floodwater.

options.feedback: 'At' shows a place or time, not the doer.
'Of' does not introduce the doer after a passive.
Correct: 'by' introduces what did the action: submerged by floodwater.
'For' shows purpose, not what did the action.

hint: After a passive verb, which word introduces the thing that did the action?
why: After a passive, 'by' introduces the doer or cause: the floodwater swept the cars away.

stem: The old embankment is now seen ____ a symbol of the 2011 floods.

options.feedback: Correct: 'be seen as' + a role or symbol.
'By' would introduce a person who sees it. A symbol is a role, so use 'as'.
'Be seen for' is not used to give a role.
We say 'be seen as', not 'be seen like'.

hint: Is 'a symbol' the doer, or the role the embankment has?
why: After 'seen, regarded, known, described' we use 'as' + the role. 'By' would only introduce the people who do the seeing.

stem: Which sentence is the most natural in a news report?

options.feedback: Correct: the repairers are obvious, so the 'by' phrase is dropped.

options.text: The road repaired yesterday by people.
options.feedback: This needs 'was', and 'by people' adds nothing.

options.text: Someone was repaired the road yesterday.
options.feedback: 'Was' should not be here: Someone repaired the road.

options.text: The road was repaired by someone yesterday.
options.feedback: 'By someone' adds no information. Drop it.

hint: Does the 'by' phrase tell the reader anything new?
why: Most passives drop the agent. 'By someone' or 'by people' adds nothing, so the natural choice is: The road was repaired yesterday.

stem: In which sentence is the 'by' phrase most useful?

options.text: The thief was arrested by the police last night.
options.feedback: Only the police arrest people, so 'by the police' adds nothing.

options.text: The new pump was designed by two SW students.
options.feedback: Correct: the designers are surprising, new information, so 'by' is worth keeping.

options.text: The letters were delivered by the postman this morning.
options.feedback: Of course the postman delivered them. The 'by' phrase adds nothing.

options.text: The injured were treated by medical staff at the hospital.
options.feedback: At a hospital, medical staff treat the injured; the 'by' phrase is obvious.

hint: Which doer would surprise a reader?
why: Keep 'by' only when the doer is new or important information. Two school students designing a pump is surprising; the others are obvious.

stem: These photos of the flooded hospital ____ a Grade 11 student.

options.feedback: Photos cannot take anything. Add be: were taken by.
'Took' is V2. The V3 of take is taken.
Correct: the photos received the action, and the student did it: were taken by.
be + V-ing is active. Use were taken by.

hint: Photos do not take anything. What is the third form of 'take'?
why: The photos received the action and the student did it, so: were + taken + by. 'Take' is irregular: take – took – taken.

stem: The shelter at our school ____ by volunteers from the parents' club.

options.feedback: 'Ran' is V2. Run is irregular: run – ran – run.
Correct: present simple passive: is + run (V3).
Without 'been' this is active: the shelter ran something. Use is run.
This makes the shelter the doer. It is run by volunteers.

hint: 'Run' is irregular. What is its third form?
why: Volunteers do the action and the shelter receives it: is + run. The verb is irregular: run – ran – run.

stem: The elderly man was carried to safety ____ two soldiers.

options.feedback: 'At' shows place or time, not the doer.
'Of' cannot introduce the doer of a passive.
Correct: 'by' introduces the people who did the carrying.
'For' shows purpose or who benefits, not the doer.

hint: Which word after a passive tells us who did it?
why: 'Was carried' is passive, and the soldiers did the carrying, so 'by' introduces them.

stem: Which headline tells the most surprising story?

options.text: Boy, 6, saved from canal by police
options.feedback: Police rescues are expected, not surprising.

options.text: Boy, 6, saved from canal by neighbour
options.feedback: A neighbour helping is kind but not surprising.

options.text: Boy, 6, saved from canal by family dog
options.feedback: Correct: a dog is a surprising rescuer, and the passive puts it at the end, where readers notice it.

options.text: Boy, 6, saved from canal by rescue team
options.feedback: Rescue teams save people every day; this doer is expected.

hint: Which doer would a reader least expect?
why: End focus: the most newsworthy information goes last. A family dog is the surprising rescuer, so the 'by' phrase is worth keeping.

stem: Extreme weather ____ Bangkok's drainage system last weekend.

options.feedback: Correct: the weather did the action, and the object (the drainage system) follows.
The sentence needs a finite verb.
This is not a complete verb form.
A passive leaves 'Bangkok's drainage system' with no role. The weather did the action.

hint: What comes right after the gap? Did the weather do something, or did something happen to it?
why: A thing can be a doer. The weather did the action and 'the drainage system' is its object, so the active past simple fits.

stem: The heavy rain ____ more than 2,000 homes in the province.

options.feedback: The sentence needs a finite verb.
Correct: the rain did the damage, and the object '2,000 homes' follows.
'The heavy rain' is singular: has.
'Damage' has only one object. A passive would leave '2,000 homes' with no role; the rain did the damage.

hint: Is there an object after the gap?
why: An object (more than 2,000 homes) follows the gap, so the subject is the doer: active present perfect, singular: has damaged.

stem: Floodwater ____ the ground floor of our house last year.

options.feedback: Correct: the water did the action, and the object (the ground floor) follows.
The sentence needs a finite verb.
This is not a complete verb form, and the water is the doer.
'Enter' has only one object. A passive would leave 'the ground floor' with no role; the water entered it.

hint: What follows the gap: an object, or nothing?
why: Floodwater did the action and 'the ground floor' is the object, so the active is correct: entered.

stem: The new tunnel ____ water from the eastern districts into the river.

options.feedback: Correct: the tunnel does the action, and 'water' is the object.
The sentence needs a finite verb.
A passive leaves 'water' with no role. The tunnel carries the water.
This is not a complete verb form.

hint: Does the tunnel do something, or does something happen to the tunnel?
why: Things can be doers. The tunnel carries the water, and 'water' follows as the object, so the active present simple is right.

stem: Volunteers repaired the canals ____ the two villages.

options.feedback: This adds a second main verb. Use a relative clause: that connect.
Correct: the canals do the connecting, and 'the two villages' is the object.
This adds a second main verb to the sentence.
The canals do the connecting; 'the two villages' is the object, so the verb is active.

hint: The sentence already has a main verb. Do the canals connect something, or are they connected?
why: 'Repaired' is the main verb, so the gap needs a relative clause. The canals connect the villages (object follows): that connect.

stem: Rising water ____ the hospital to move its patients by boat.

options.feedback: Correct: the water did the action, and 'the hospital' is its object.
The sentence needs a finite verb.
This is not a complete verb form, and the water is the doer.
'Force' has only one object here. A passive would leave 'the hospital' with no role; the water forced it.

hint: Who or what did the forcing?
why: Rising water caused the move and 'the hospital' is its object, so the active past simple fits: forced the hospital to move.

stem: The new barriers could ____ the market from future floods.

options.feedback: Correct: modal + base verb (active). The barriers protect the market.
After a modal, use the base form.
After a modal, use the base form, not -ing.
This would mean the barriers are protected, but 'the market' follows as the object.

hint: After the gap comes 'the market'. Is it the object of the barriers' action?
why: The barriers do the protecting and 'the market' is the object, so modal + active base verb: could protect.

stem: The city plans ____ three new pumping stations before the next rainy season.

options.feedback: 'Plan' is followed by a to-infinitive.
Correct: plan + to-infinitive, active: the city builds them.
'Plan' takes a to-infinitive, and the city is the doer.
This would mean the city is built. The object 'three stations' follows.

hint: Who builds the stations? What pattern follows 'plan'?
why: 'Plan' takes a to-infinitive, and the city is the doer with an object following, so the active infinitive: to build.

stem: Families ____ near the canal were the first to be evacuated.

options.feedback: 'Lived' cannot shorten 'who live'. Use 'living'.
Correct: active participle: families who live near the canal.
This adds a second main verb ('were' is the main verb).
'Live' here has no object, so it cannot be passive.

hint: Do the families do this action themselves?
why: 'Were' is the main verb, so the gap needs a reduced clause. The families live there (active), so the -ing participle: living.

stem: The floods ____ 2.45 million people in 20 provinces and Bangkok by 13 October.

options.feedback: The sentence needs a finite verb.
Correct: the floods did the action, and the object '2.45 million people' follows.
Wrong voice: the floods did the affecting.
A passive leaves '2.45 million people' with no role. The floods affected the people.

hint: Is there an object after the gap?
why: The floods are the doer and '2.45 million people' is the object, so the active past perfect (before 13 October) is right.

stem: Residents complained about the authorities ____ them too late.

options.feedback: After a preposition, use the -ing form.
Correct: after 'about', a gerund. The authorities warned them: active.
After a preposition (about), use -ing, not to.
The authorities did the warning, and 'them' is the object, so the gerund is active.

hint: Who gave the message, and what form follows a preposition?
why: After a preposition we use a gerund. 'The authorities' do the warning and 'them' is the object, so the active gerund: warning.

stem: Every rainy season, the river ____ the fields near our grandmother's house.

options.feedback: Correct: the river does the action, and 'the fields' is its object.
The sentence needs a finite verb.
A passive leaves 'the fields' with no role. The river floods the fields.
Not a complete verb form.

hint: What follows the gap?
why: The river is the doer and 'the fields' is the object, so the active present simple (a regular event) fits: floods.

stem: Residents near the canal have been advised ____ their motorbikes to higher ground.

options.feedback: 'Be advised' is followed by a to-infinitive.
Correct: the residents move their motorbikes (object follows): active to-infinitive.
After 'to', use the base form.
This would mean the residents are moved, but 'their motorbikes' follows as the object.

hint: Who will do the moving? What comes after the gap?
why: 'Have been advised' is passive, but the residents do the moving and 'their motorbikes' is the object, so the active infinitive: to move.

stem: The floodwater finally ____ last Sunday.

options.feedback: 'Last Sunday' is past, so use the past simple: subsided.
Correct: 'subside' has no object, so it is always active.
'Subside' never takes an object, so it has no passive.
No passive is possible, and 'last Sunday' needs the past simple.

hint: Can you subside something? If a verb has no object, can it be passive?
why: 'Subside' (go down) never takes an object, so it cannot be passive. 'Last Sunday' needs the past simple: subsided.

stem: The water level in the Chao Phraya ____ by 30 cm overnight.

options.feedback: Correct: 'rise' has no object and no passive: rise – rose – risen.
'Risen' is a past participle; the sentence needs a finite verb: rose.
'Raise' needs an object (raise the level). Here nothing follows, so use 'rose'.
'Rise' never takes an object, so it cannot be passive.

hint: Rise or raise? Which one needs an object?
why: 'Rise' (go up by itself) has no object and no passive; 'raise' needs an object. Nothing follows the gap, so: rose.

stem: The accident ____ when a truck tried to drive through deep water.

options.feedback: Correct: 'happen' has no object, so it is always active.
'Happen' has no passive form.
'Happen' never takes an object, so it has no passive.
No passive is possible with 'happen'.

hint: Can you 'happen' something?
why: Happen, occur, appear, die and arrive have no object, so they have no passive. The past simple active is right: happened.

stem: When the power came back, the ice in the freezer had already ____.

options.feedback: After 'had', use the past participle.
Correct: the ice melted by itself, so the active is used.
After 'had', use the past participle: had melted.
Nobody melted the ice; it changed by itself, so no passive.

hint: Did someone melt the ice, or did it melt by itself?
why: 'Melt' can be active or passive. With no outside doer (it melted by itself), use the active: had melted.

stem: At least 31 people ____ in the floods by early October.

options.feedback: Correct: 'die' has no object, so it is always active.
This says the people killed someone. 'Kill' needs an object.
'Die' has no passive.
'Die' never takes an object, so it has no passive. (Killed can be passive.)

hint: Does 'die' ever take an object? (Compare 'kill'.)
why: 'Die' has no object, so no passive. If you want a passive, change the verb: were killed. Here the active past perfect: had died.

stem: Large cracks ____ in the school wall after the flood.

options.feedback: Correct: 'appear' has no object, so it is always active.
'Appear' has no passive.
'Appear' never takes an object, so it has no passive.
No passive is possible with 'appear'.

hint: Can you 'appear' something?
why: 'Appear' is one of the verbs learners often make passive by mistake. It has no object, so: appeared.

stem: The crowd outside the shelter ____ quickly as the water rose.

options.feedback: Correct: the crowd grew by itself, so the active is used.
The sentence needs a finite verb.
'Grew' is V2, and the crowd grew by itself (active).
Nobody grew the crowd; it changed by itself.

hint: Did someone grow the crowd, or did it grow by itself?
why: 'Grow' is passive only with an outside doer (rice is grown). A crowd grows by itself, so the active past simple: grew.

stem: Many fish ____ when the dirty floodwater reached the pond.

options.feedback: Correct: 'die' has no object, so it is always active.
'Dead' is an adjective; the sentence needs a verb.
The sentence needs a finite verb: died.
'Die' never takes an object, so it cannot be passive.

hint: Can 'die' be passive?
why: 'Die' has no object, so it has no passive form. The past simple active is correct: died.

stem: Rescue boats ____ at the village two hours after the call.

options.feedback: Correct: 'arrive' has no object and takes 'at'.
'Reach' takes a direct object: reached the village (no 'at').
'Arrive' has no object, so it has no passive.
This means someone reached the boats; and 'reach' takes no 'at'.

hint: Look at 'at' after the gap. Which verb is followed by 'at'?
why: 'Arrive at' + place has no object and no passive; 'reach' takes a direct object with no preposition. So: arrived.

stem: Most of the boats used in the rescue ____ to local fishermen.

options.feedback: Correct: 'belong' is a state verb with no passive.
'Belong' has no passive form.
'Belong' is a state verb; it is not used in the continuous here.
'Belong' has no passive.

hint: What kind of verb is this: an action or a state?
why: State verbs like belong, resemble, lack and suit have no passive. The past simple active fits: belonged to.

stem: Problems with the drains ____ every time it rains heavily.

options.feedback: Correct: 'occur' has no object, so it is active; plural subject 'problems'.
The subject is 'problems' (plural), so the verb is 'occur', not 'occurs'.
'Occur' never takes an object, so it has no passive.
No passive with 'occur'.

hint: Find the real subject. Can this verb take an object?
why: 'Occur' has no passive, and the subject is 'problems' (plural), so the present simple active plural: occur.

stem: The dam release is expected to ____ the river level by another 20 cm.

options.feedback: 'Rise' has no object. Here 'the river level' follows, so use 'raise'.
Correct: 'raise' takes an object (the river).
'Rise' has no passive.
This would mean the release is raised, but 'the river level' follows as the object.

hint: Is there an object after the gap? Which of the two similar verbs needs one?
why: 'The river level' is an object, so we need 'raise' (transitive). 'Rise' has no object and no passive.

stem: Each family at the shelter ____ a relief bag yesterday.

options.feedback: This means the family gave a bag to someone: the opposite meaning.
'Gave' is V2. The V3 of give is given.
Correct: the person is the subject: Each family was given a bag.
This means the family was giving a bag to someone.

hint: Did the family give the bag, or receive it?
why: 'Give' has two objects (someone something). The person can be the subject of the passive: Each family was given a relief bag.

stem: New volunteers ____ how to use the pumps by experienced staff.

options.feedback: This means the volunteers show someone: the opposite meaning.
Correct: 'show' can make the person the passive subject.
This means the volunteers are showing someone.
'Explain' cannot take the person as object: something is explained TO someone.

hint: Which verbs can have the person as the subject of a passive?
why: 'Show' takes two objects, so 'Volunteers are shown how…' works. 'Explain' cannot: we say 'it is explained to them'.

stem: The situation ____ by a nurse, who was very kind.

options.feedback: The sentence needs a finite verb: was described.
'Describe' cannot take the person as a direct object; use 'to me'.
This means the situation was describing me.
Correct: 'describe' needs 'to' + person.

hint: Can 'describe' be followed directly by a person?
why: Describe, explain, suggest and mention take 'to' + person: The situation was described to me. They cannot take the person as a direct object.

stem: Thousands of displaced residents have been ____ free meals since last week.

options.feedback: After 'been', use V3.
Correct: the person is the subject: residents have been offered meals.
After 'have been', use V3 for a passive.
With the person as subject, no 'to' is needed before the thing.

hint: The residents receive the meals. What form follows 'have been'?
why: 'Offer' has two objects, so the person can be the passive subject: residents have been offered free meals.
